text:
maria: Quick sync — proposing final metric defs for the runtime dashboard so dashboards, alerts, and PR checks all use the same terms. Main items: 1) TTFT = time-to-first-model-token measured from when request is received by the edge/router to when the runtime emits the first non-empty model token. Exclude LB queuing where measurable; include runtime scheduling and kernel time. 2) tokens/s = token generation rate averaged over the active generation window for the request (exclude padding and idle heartbeats). 3) latency_p95_ms = 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency (request receipt -> final token emitted). Also add error_rate (5xx/timeout), cold_start_count, and seq_len_histogram. Doc: https://redwood.example.com/internal/metrics/metric-specs (WIP)

kevin: SGTM on the high level. Quick q — for TTFT do we treat function_call responses (structured JSON) the same as text streams? I think we should define "first logical token" (first non-empty payload) across formats. Also how do we treat empty streaming chunks used as keep-alives?

anna: Agree on "first logical token" for formats. For streaming empty chunks (keep-alive), TTFT should ignore zero-content frames — filter by content_length > 0 or first_token_length > 0. Also propose we emit two related metrics for debugging: ttft_ms (measured at runtime) and client_first_byte_ms (measured at proxy/client) so we can separate network vs model issues.

perf-bot: perf-bot: benchmark run 1767609988 completed. Summary: model-rwkv-13b q8: ttft p50=85ms p95=210ms tokens_s.request=420 tokens_s.pool=10240 errors=0. Full results: /runs/1767609988.csv

leo: Nice. For tokens/s we should expose both per-request (tokens_s.request) and aggregate throughput across the serving pool (tokens_s.pool). Also add model_variant and seq_len_histogram to the time series so we can slice by prompt length and variant.

maria: Good call. I'll add fields: tokens_s.request, tokens_s.pool, model_variant, seq_len_histogram. Also store latency_p50/p80/p95/p99 as separate fields rather than only p95 — that helps triage. Storing raw p95 as "latency_p95_ms" and a bucketed count for common ranges. Any objections?

kevin: No objections. For alerts: propose alert rule — if latency_p95_ms > 500 for 5m -> page oncall. For PR/regression gating: if latency_p95_ms increases >15% vs baseline for the model tag (baseline window = last 7 days) -> fail CI and notify @eng-runtime. We need sampling and an agreed baseline window in the CI harness.

anna: I'll update dashboard JSON and create the alert rules. I'll also wire the regression hook into prow/perf-tests — will add a small CI shim to compare baseline. Assigning the metrics lib change to myself to expose tokens_s.request.

maria: Thanks — I'll open the PR that updates the metrics schema + docs and include the new dashboard panels and alert definitions. Reviewers: @kevin and @leo. ETA: PR tomorrow EOD. I'll also add a short runbook for triage steps (how to interpret ttft vs client_first_byte).

kevin: :thumbsup: Will review. One more ask from perf: can the team run a profiling pass on the canary cluster with the golden prompt set after the PR merges? Need flame graphs and kernel hotspots. Window ~2h.

perf-bot: perf-bot: scheduled profiling job 1767610200 started on canary. Artifacts will upload to /artifacts/1767610200/ when finished.

leo: One small nit — in the UI let's label the metric "Time to first model token" for clarity, but keep the metric key as ttft_ms in telemetry to avoid churn.

maria: Sound plan. I'll make those naming choices in the PR and update the docs. Thanks everyone — will follow up with the PR link here.
